result:
Solution 1 is correct, but I did not verify the "only if" direction myself; that rests on my recollection of the published result.

**Power-solution reduction.** Try u = c·x_nᵝ, extended by 0 for x_n ≤ 0. Matching exponents in (−Δ)ˢu = x_nᵅu^(−γ) gives β − 2s = α − γβ, so β = (α + 2s)/(1 + γ).

**Sign of the constant.** (−Δ)ˢ(x_n⁺)ᵝ = Λ(β)·x_n^(β−2s), where Λ(β) > 0 exactly for β ∈ (s−1, s). Solving for c > 0 requires Λ(β) > 0.

**Why the lower end is 0, not s−1.** The Dirichlet condition requires u to vanish on the boundary, so β > 0. Exponents in (s−1, 0] give functions that blow up or stay nonzero at the boundary, so they are excluded. The admissible range is therefore β ∈ (0, s).

**Resulting interval.** 0 < (α + 2s)/(1 + γ) < s is equivalent to −2s < α < s(γ − 1). So A = −2s and B = s(γ − 1), giving A + B = s(γ − 3).

**Why Solutions 2 and 3 fail.** They use the interval β ∈ (s−1, s) and so take A = (s−1)(1+γ) − 2s. That allows β ≤ 0 and violates the Dirichlet condition.

CHOICE: 1
